claims: Every plumbing employee gets an industry allowance ($41.41 a week) and a special fixed allowance ($7.70); tradespersons also get the plumbing trade allowance ($33.57)
Every plumbing employee gets ... a special fixed allowance ($7.70); tradespersons also get the plumbing trade allowance ($33.57)
whys: This conflicts with the page's own allowance table and the file header. The special fixed allowance goes to all employees except apprentices (cl 21.3(d), line 141), and the plumbing trade allowance also goes to plumbing worker level 2 (cl 21.3(b), line 139). I left the wording alone because the brief says not to change facts. A suggested fix: 'every employee except an apprentice gets a special fixed allowance', and 'worker level 2 and tradespersons get the plumbing trade allowance'.

This conflicts with the page's own allowance notes (lines 139 and 141) and the workers table intro (line 107). The special fixed allowance excludes apprentices (cl 21.3(d)), and worker level 2 also gets the plumbing trade allowance (cl 21.3(b)).
reviewerNotes: I agree with the writer's question. The coverage paragraph says every plumbing employee gets the special fixed allowance and only tradespersons get the plumbing trade allowance. That conflicts with the allowances[] notes in plumber.ts (lines 139 and 141), which apply the special fixed allowance to everyone except apprentices (cl 21.3(d)) and also pay the plumbing trade allowance to worker level 2 (cl 21.3(b)). Under the brief this is a human fact decision, so I left the text as it is.

claims: An assistant, deputy or second-in-charge manager is graded one step below the manager they assist: Level 4 in a shop without departments, Level 6 in a shop with departments.
whys: The levels given are two classification levels below the manager (Level 6 to Level 4, Level 8 to Level 6), and Levels 5 and 7 exist between them, so 'one step below' reads as wrong. The Level 4 and Level 6 figures themselves match Schedule A.4.3 and A.6.2 as quoted in the file header. I did not change the wording because the fix removes or changes a count.
constants: Schedule A.4.3 / A.6.2 indicative titles (header comment of retail-manager.ts)
reviewerNotes: The writer's fact question is valid. 'One step below' does not match the Schedule A levels the coverage line gives: Level 6 to Level 4 and Level 8 to Level 6 are two levels apart. Left for a human to decide.

claims: Vets employed by government, universities or under an enterprise agreement may be paid under other instruments.
whys: This is a hedged coverage rule. The sibling vet-nurse page says definitively that university and government staff fall outside the award, which covers private practices and charities only. The two pages should agree. I left the wording as it is because removing 'may' would be a new factual claim.

Vehicle manufacturing is a stream within the Manufacturing Award (Schedule B, V levels), and the same page says so at lines 82 and 101. MA000010 coverage also appears to include ship building and repair. Naming both as 'a different award' contradicts the page.
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's question. coverage[2] lists vehicle manufacturing (and shipbuilding) as possibly falling under 'a different award'. The same page (line 82, Schedule B V levels; FAQ line 101 'V2 and V3 in vehicle manufacturing') treats vehicle manufacturing as a stream inside MA000010, so the page contradicts itself. This needs an owner or fact check. The string was not changed in this pass.
